newsitem.title: USA: Bellsouth files challenge to FCC phone rules.
newsitem.headline: Bellsouth files challenge to FCC phone rules.

text.p: Bellsouth Corp said Friday it had asked the U.S. Court of Appeals here to overturn major parts of the Federal Communications Commission's new rules designed to open the local phone market to competition.

The company joins a growing list of local phone providers, including U S West Inc, Pacific Telesis Group and Bell Atlantic Corp and state regulators who are challenging the FCC's "interconnection" rules in court.
BellSouth said it will argue that the FCC had no right to supplant marketplace agreements or "the intent of Congress with its minutely detailed rules."

"The Commission seems to be taking over regulation of local telephony which is entrusted to the states," BellSouth general counsel Walter Alford said in a statement, adding "This does not square with the regulatory intent of Congress."
Lawyers predict the challenges will fail and that the main portions of the rules will survive in court.
Major long-distance companies have not formally challenged the new rules.
